source.title: Implicit Regularization via Neural Feature Alignment
source.authors: A. Baratin; Thomas George; César Laurent; R. Devon Hjelm; Guillaume Lajoie; Pascal Vincent; Simon Lacoste-Julien

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies MLP width and compares the generalization gap, but does not test the original claim's exact setup or report extractable numerical results for that sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports alignment and effective-rank findings, but these do not test the specific versions except for the width sweep relevant to V2. Cited results from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: Figure 6 measures training and test error while varying MNIST MLP width at a common training cross-entropy of 0.01, bearing on V2. The supplied text does not preserve the plotted curves well enough to establish the direction of test error as width increases.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret task-dependent tangent-feature alignment as feature selection and compression, motivate it as implicit regularization, and report that their heuristic complexity measure tracks generalization gaps across parameter counts and label corruption. They do not establish a general neural-network generalization bound for that heuristic.
record.recipe_differences: Studies tangent-feature alignment and a proposed complexity measure; it does not reproduce the specified original interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that alignment effects vary with depth and learning rate; increasing learning rate tends to enhance alignment, while reducing it yields a higher effective-rank value in the illustrated setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under high label noise, VGG19 tangent-kernel effective rank decreases as test accuracy improves and rises when overfitting begins.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tangent-kernel effective rank tracks learning and overfitting in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that their trajectory-based complexity measure reflects the generalization-gap shape across parameter counts and label-corruption levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A complexity measure combining SGD-update norms and tangent-feature norms can track generalization gaps in the tested settings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2021), PMLR Volume 130
record.problems: The width-sweep error results are shown in a figure without numerical values in the text. The effective-rank relationship is reported qualitatively and is correlational.

untested.parts: The experiments include partially corrupted labels, but do not establish the complete comparison involving almost-perfect fitting of fully random labels and chance held-out accuracy.
The supplied text does not establish exactly zero training error, locate the interpolation threshold, or reveal the subsequent test-error trend. Downsampled CIFAR-10 MLP results are not reported.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected classifiers, local connectivity, or transferred convolutional initialization.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of its ranking with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence and retraining comparison.

missing.what: The VGG19 channel-width sweep reports training and test error at cross-entropy 0.01 but has no result row. Record this additional width setting; its test-error direction cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source listed for the versions. No directional V2 verdict is justified by the supplied text: the statement that a complexity measure reflects the gap's shape does not specify that shape. Figure-only unreadability is an evidence limitation, not a demonstrated limitation of V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report fitting fixed random labels nearly perfectly alongside natural-label generalization, or held-out performance on random labels.

The paper varies MLP width and plots training and test error, but the figure does not provide extractable numerical results establishing the direction of test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers as specified.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Does not vary batch size to test a large-batch generalization penalty.
Does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures as specified.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST
rows.size_stated: varying hidden layer size; up to 4 millions parameters
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden layer size and plotted training and test error.
rows.measure: training and test error / generalization gap
rows.note: The text says the proposed complexity measure reflects the shape of the generalization gap, but the plotted error values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The width intervention and error measures are relevant, but neither the post-interpolation test-error trend nor the interpolation threshold can be read from the supplied text. Cross-entropy of 0.01 does not by itself establish exactly zero training error.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Tracked tangent-kernel effective rank during training and related it to test accuracy.

conditions.value: during the learning phase and when overfitting starts

rows.value: The effective rank anticorrelates nicely with test accuracy: it decreases as test accuracy increases, then rises when overfitting starts and test accuracy decreases.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a proxy for effective capacity; it is not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: The qualitative effective-rank finding is accurately reported, but it measures none of V1–V8. Its observed correlation cannot establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
